outgoing.name: Arabic language
outgoing.excerpt: The Radhanites (also Radanites; Hebrew sing. רדהני, Radhani, pl. רדהנים Radhanim; Arabic الرذنية, ar-Raðaniyya) were medieval Jewish merchants.

outgoing.name: China
outgoing.excerpt: Their trade network covered much of Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia and parts of India and China.

outgoing.name: Europe
outgoing.excerpt: Their trade network covered much of Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia and parts of India and China.

outgoing.name: Genoa
outgoing.section: The end of the Radhanite age
outgoing.excerpt: This period saw the rise of the mercantile Italian city-states, especially Genoa, Venice, Pisa, and Amalfi, who viewed the Radhanites as unwanted competitors.

outgoing.excerpt: Some scholars believe that the Radhanites may have played a role in the conversion of the Khazars to Judaism.

outgoing.name: Kiev
outgoing.excerpt: Sefer ha-Dinim, a Hebrew account of the travels of Yehuda ben Meir of Mainz, named Przemyśl and Kiev as trading sites along the Radhanite route.
